text:
maya: seeing p99 jump on pool-c around 18:05 UTC, started ~18:02, coincides with a burst from tenant-47
jorge: yep, I see the traces too — tail latency up ~3x for a handful of tenants, overall throughput down ~12%
devon: any recent rollout or kernel changes?
infra-bot: deploy: inference-runtime v1.13.2 rolled to pool-c at 17:58 UTC (config: batching-v2, kernel-autoswitch=on) :information_source:
maya: not from our side, no canary. suspect noisy neighbor / resource thrash
jorge: ran a quick profiler on a sampled request set from tenant-47 vs tenant-21. interesting bits:
```
profile summary:
- tenant-47: matmul kernel selection oscillating between matmul_tiled_v2 and matmul_tiled_v3 (hot switch at seq_len=512)
- tenant-21: stable matmul_tiled_v3
- batching: tenant-47 often triggers small micro-batches (batch_size 1-4) causing kernel warmup penalties
- kv-cache: tenant-47 has a high eviction rate ~22% per-minute vs baseline 3%
p99 latency delta: tenant-47 +420ms
```
jorge: looks like two things: kernel thrash from oscillation + kv-cache thrash causing more cache misses and L2 pressure
anika: that eviction rate is alarming — tenant-47's prompt patterns are highly variable, probing many prefixes. our default kv-slot config is 128 slots on pool-c, might be causing cross-tenant eviction contention
ryan: could be exacerbated by batching heuristic: batching-v2 tries to pack across tenants to maximize throughput. when one tenant has many short sequences it unbalances kernel selection and causes slow paths
devon: can we repro locally with recorded traces? I can replay tenant-47's traffic against pool-c nodes with current runtime flags
maya: yes please, devon. i saved a 10m capture and uploaded to /mnt/profiles/tenant-47-1802.tar.gz
jorge: to speed mitigation, propose immediate config changes (can roll forward):
- force per-tenant batching isolation = true (disable cross-tenant packing)
- bump kv-slot-per-tenant to 512 on pool-c for next 2 hours
- pin kernel for model-x to matmul_tiled_v3 when seq_len >= 256 to avoid oscillation
- reduce per-tenant inflight to 120 requests (soft throttle)
ryan: :+1: I can push a canary of those flags to 10% of pool-c in 5m, monitor p95/p99
infra-bot: change_request: batching_isolation=true, kv_slots=512, kernel_pin=matmul_tiled_v3, inflight_limit=120 -> canary(10%) at 18:20 UTC
sre-bot: alert: p99 for pool-c dropped 30% after canary rollout :white_check_mark:
maya: after canary we saw tenant-47 p99 go down ~260ms and overall pool-c throughput back up ~7%
jorge: devon, once you have the replay results, please run a profiler with kernel selection tracing enabled (trace.kernels=1) and KV eviction sampling (kv.sample_rate=0.1)
devon: will do. running now, ETA ~12m
anika: follow-up: we should add a scheduled job that computes per-tenant kv working set and recommends slots automatically. manual bumps are fine short-term but we need adaptive quotas
ryan: agree. short-term mitigation = roll-forward config across pool-c. medium-term = adaptive kv allocator + batching heuristic that prefers tenant-local groups
maya: i'll open a post-incident action item and assign:
- devon: replay + kernel trace (due EOD)
- jorge: write a short runbook for kernel-pinning heuristics (due tomorrow)
- anika: prototype kv working-set estimator (PR by next week)
- ryan: follow up on rollout metrics and revert plan (monitoring dashboard)
maya: thanks all. labeling incident: INC-2026-pool-c-tenant-interference. i'll update exec thread once we confirm full roll-forward :rocket:
ryan: quick note — let's add a guard to avoid pinning kernels globally; pinning should be per-model+tenant when heuristic confidence > 0.8
jorge: good call. we'll make the pin decision gated by confidence score
devon: profiler finished — attaching flamegraph: https://profiles.redwood.internal/fg/1924680000/tenant-47.html 
maya: grabbing the flamegraph now. initial glance shows hot path in matmul tiling transition and a spike in L2 cache misses matching eviction spikes
maya: closing loop: canary to 10% at 18:20, full roll to 100% at 18:28 after green signals. follow-ups tracked in INC-2026. :memo:
